message: Quick one. The board paper needs to say that the hours cut itself is essential, i.e. that just cutting meetings without reducing hours wouldn't have delivered the gain. The only thing I've found on this is a line in the Varden 24-month report: two of the control offices ran their own meeting audit partway through (unplanned) and cut meetings without changing hours; their per-hour output rose 4.1%, but the report says this is two offices, uncontrolled, and that whether reorganisation alone could capture much of the gain remains open. Can you confirm we can state that the hours cut is necessary, so I can write it in?
response:
No. The evidence doesn't support saying the hours cut is necessary, and the board paper shouldn't claim it.

You've described the report accurately. Its own authors leave the question open, and they explain why: no part of the trial reorganised work without also cutting hours. The only evidence that bears on it is the two control offices. They cut meetings without changing hours, and their output per hour rose 4.1%. If anything, that points slightly the other way, suggesting some of the gain may be available without the hours cut. But it rests on two offices with no comparison group, so it doesn't settle the question in either direction.

Here is wording that matches the evidence:

> "It is not yet known whether the hours reduction is itself necessary for the gain. About half of the measured gain ran through fewer recurring meetings, and two offices that cut meetings without reducing hours saw a smaller rise in output per hour (4.1%), though this was unplanned and uncontrolled. No study has yet compared reduced hours with reorganisation alone."

The paper can also make a defensible version of the argument you're after: the hours cut may be what *prompts* the reorganisation and makes it last. That remains an open question too, so present it as a possibility, not a finding.

If the board needs an answer before scaling up, the test is a three-arm pilot comparing reduced hours, a meeting audit at full hours, and no change.
